messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in container restarts for svc-gpu-cluster-a (oom_kill events). Alert ID: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts/6299990000
ashley: noticed ~200 restarts in the last 10m. kube events show OOMKilled (exit code 137). Paging oncall now.
sam: pasting runtime excerpt: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating 2147483648 bytes` then process exits. also seeing `killed process 23456` from kernel logs.
lee: correlation with traffic -> sudden increase in very long prefill requests (client header x-context-tokens ~120k). prefill path allocates KV cache + attention buffers proportional to sequence length.
maria: CS: two customers showing elevated 5xx errors, one is production (vertiq-ads). They've opened live tickets.
kai: product question: can we drop them to a smaller model variant automatically? Need to avoid impacting normal traffic.
jen: ops suggestion: short-term: apply a non-invasive prefill clamp that truncates prefill to 32k tokens with graceful truncation notice header. mid-term: implement prefill streaming and on-the-fly KV allocation.
ashley: applying clamp now: `redwoodctl cfg set --service svc-gpu-cluster-a prefill.clamp_tokens=32768 --dry-run=false` rolling config applied. also adding a route rule to send >32k to cpu-pool: `redwoodctl route update --expr "req.headers['x-context-tokens'] > 32768" --to cpu-pool`
incident-bot: config change submitted by ashley at 6299990035  change id: cfg-8712
sam: after the clamp, restart rate dropped by ~70%. still seeing a tail of restarts from pre-existing pods that haven't rotated.
lee: looking at the runtime allocator: we pre-allocate contiguous GPU buffers for KV cache which fragments under many different sizes. quick fix: switch allocator to 'sparse' mode to reduce contiguous allocation size. I'll toggle the allocator flag.
jen: note: sparse allocator may slightly increase per-token latency for small contexts, but reduces OOM risk. Ops queue it as a short blip.
maria: sent customer update: "We observed large prompts causing GPU memory exhaustion. We've applied temporary limits and routing to mitigate. We'll follow up with timeline and root cause."
kai: okay to send. include guidance for customers that if they need larger windows they can request private-dedicated capacity.
lee: toggled allocator: `redwoodctl runtime set --name svc-gpu-cluster-a --set allocator.mode=sparse` and restarted nodes gracefully.
ashley: we're also bumping node pool scale by +20% to absorb residual load: `k scale nodepool gpu-a --replicas +20%`
sam: logs now show far fewer CUDA OOMs. a few remaining hot pods show fragmentation traces; I've evicted them.
jen: filed follow-ups: (1) runtime: implement on-demand KV growth with cap and truncation (lee/sam), (2) platform: add tenant-level large-context quota and billing guardrails (kai/product), (3) SRE: enhance alert to include median prefill token size (ashley/ops).
lee: collecting heap / GPU traces from one noisy container: `nvidia-smi topo --filename /tmp/topo; python -m tracemalloc --output /tmp/trace` will ship to s3.
maria: incident ticket INC-8342 created with impacted customer list and times. CS will coordinate refunds if SLA breach confirmed.
ashley: handing off to oncall lee for overnight monitoring. I'm documenting mitigations and steps to roll back changes if we see latency regressions.
lee: ack. I'll monitor pod restarts, OOM logs, and alert if restart rate exceeds baseline. leaving this thread open and will post hourly updates.
incident-bot: incident state -> mitigated (partial) at 6299990123. Logs and incident timeline: https://incidents.redwood.internal/6299990000
ashley: thanks team. follow-ups assigned; will run postmortem after stable. :thumbsup:
